title: Swelling and Asymmetry After Breast Augmentation: FAQ
meta_title: Breast Augmentation Swelling Asymmetry: What's Normal?
meta_description: Breast augmentation swelling asymmetry is common early in recovery. Learn what is normal, when to call your surgeon, and how healing progresses safely.
excerpt: One breast may look higher, firmer, or more swollen as your body heals after breast augmentation. Learn why uneven swelling happens, what to expect by week, and when changing symptoms warrant a call to your surgical team.
quick_answer:
Is it normal for one breast to be higher after breast augmentation?

Usually, in the first weeks. University of Utah Health says each breast may heal at a different rate, and The Aesthetic Society says most residual swelling resolves within a month. An article on the ASPS website says drop and fluff can take 3 to 6 months. Call your surgeon the same day if one side suddenly grows or hardens.

A note says chest pain or trouble breathing means the emergency room. Sources: Cleveland Clinic, MedlinePlus and University of Utah Health.
